faq.heading: FAQ
faq.subheading: Common questions about security and privacy
faq.safeQ: Is it safe to connect my Telegram?
faq.safeA: Yes. Your account connects via QR code — the same flow Telegram Web and Desktop use, so you stay in control. Read-only tools work out of the box. Write tools (send a reply, react, save a draft) are available so the AI can act on your behalf when you ask it to. Irreversible actions (delete, edit, kick) are off by default and require an explicit opt-in in your settings, with a daily quota and an audit log. You can disconnect or revoke the session at any time from Telegram → Settings → Devices.
faq.readQ: Can you read my messages on the server?
faq.readAStart: We don't store your messages. Each tool call fetches data directly from Telegram's API and returns it to the AI assistant. Your Telegram session key is stored on our server so the connector can keep working between requests, and is deleted whenever your session ends (see the next answer for the exact timing). Storage details and hardening guidance are in our
faq.protocolQ: How does it connect without the Bot API?
faq.protocolA: It uses MTProto — the same protocol Telegram's official apps use. You authenticate via QR code, just like linking a new device. From Telegram's perspective, it's another logged-in client.
faq.disconnectA: If you explicitly remove the connector in Claude.ai or ChatGPT, the server logs the Telegram session out and deletes the session key right away. If you just close the AI app without revoking, the in-memory client is dropped immediately and the stored session key is kept briefly so you can resume seamlessly; if you don't reconnect within a short idle window (a few minutes), the server logs out and deletes the key automatically. You can also force a full revoke at any time from Telegram → Settings → Devices.
faq.chatgptAStart: Yes. Add it as an app in ChatGPT Settings → Apps (Developer Mode). Use the URL
faq.chatgptAEnd: with OAuth authentication. Works on Plus, Pro, Team, and Enterprise plans.
faq.openSourceAStart: Yes. The server is fully open-source under the MIT license at
faq.multiAccountQ: Can I connect more than one Telegram account?
faq.multiAccountA: Yes. After connecting your first account, ask the assistant to add another with the `telegram-accounts-add` tool — you'll get a one-time URL with a QR code for the second account. Use `telegram-accounts-switch` to change which account the next tool call will use. No disconnect/reconnect needed.

examplesPage.metaTitle: Examples — What people ask Claude AI & ChatGPT about Telegram
examplesPage.metaDescription: 12 ready-to-use prompts for Claude AI and ChatGPT to read your Telegram chats: morning briefings, finding messages, extracting data, people lookup, and more.
examplesPage.heading: Real-world examples
examplesPage.subheading: Twelve ready-to-paste prompts. Each one works after connecting Telegram via Quickstart.

morning.title: Morning briefing
morning.description: A daily summary of unread chats, with urgent items pulled to the top.
morning.prompt: Summarize my unread Telegram messages from the last 12 hours. Group them by chat, highlight anything that mentions "urgent", "deadline", or a date in the next 48 hours, and list any direct questions addressed to me.

weeklyDigest.title: Weekly digest from a busy channel
weeklyDigest.description: Catch up on a noisy channel without scrolling through hundreds of posts.
weeklyDigest.prompt: Look at the last 7 days of messages in my "AI News" Telegram channel. Give me 5 bullet points of the most-discussed topics, with one example link per topic.

findDeadline.title: Find that deadline message
findDeadline.description: Locate a specific past message without remembering the exact words.
findDeadline.prompt: Find the message in our work chat where someone mentioned the project deadline. Show me the date, who sent it, and 2 messages of context before and after.

findFiles.title: Find shared documents
findFiles.description: List every file someone shared in a chat over a date range.
findFiles.prompt: Show me all PDF and DOCX attachments shared in the "Design Team" Telegram chat in the last 30 days, sorted newest first, with the file name and who sent it.

linksThisWeek.title: All links shared this week
linksThisWeek.description: Build a reading list from links your community shared.
linksThisWeek.prompt: List every URL shared in the "Reading Group" Telegram channel this week. Deduplicate, group by domain, and add the message timestamp for each.

extractActions.title: Extract action items
extractActions.description: Turn an informal chat thread into a TODO list.
extractActions.prompt: Read the last 50 messages in my team chat and extract any action items. For each action, include the assignee, the deadline if mentioned, and a one-line description.

topMembers.title: Most active community members
topMembers.description: Spot helpers and leaders in a community group.
topMembers.prompt: In our community Telegram group, list the top 10 most active members of the last 30 days. For each, show how many messages they sent and one representative recent message.

whoMentioned.title: Who mentioned me
whoMentioned.description: Find messages that addressed you directly.
whoMentioned.prompt: Show me all messages from the last 7 days where someone mentioned me by @username or replied directly to one of my messages. Group by chat.

chatActivity.title: Chat activity over time
chatActivity.description: See when a chat is busy and quiet.
chatActivity.prompt: For my "Engineering Team" chat, show message counts per day for the last 14 days. Tell me which days had unusual spikes or silences.

unreadByChat.title: Unread by chat
unreadByChat.description: Triage your inbox with one prompt.
unreadByChat.prompt: List all my Telegram chats that have unread messages right now, sorted by unread count descending. For each, show the chat name and the first 3 unread messages.

photosFamily.title: Recent family photos
photosFamily.description: Pull recent shared photos and view them inline.
photosFamily.prompt: Show me the photos sent in the "Family" Telegram chat in the last 3 days. Display them inline with the date and who sent each photo.

voiceTranscripts.title: Transcripts of voice messages
voiceTranscripts.description: Skim long voice notes by reading them as text.
voiceTranscripts.prompt: Find all voice messages sent in my "Coworking" group chat this week. Transcribe each one and present them as a chronological list with sender and timestamp.

quickstart.metaTitle: Quickstart — Connect Telegram to Claude AI or ChatGPT
quickstart.metaDescription: Step-by-step guide to connect your Telegram account to Claude AI or ChatGPT in 30 seconds. QR-code login, no API keys.
quickstart.heading: Quickstart
quickstart.subheading: Connect your Telegram in under a minute. Pick your AI assistant below.
quickstart.tabClaudeDesc: Add the connector in claude.ai · 5 steps · ~30 seconds
quickstart.tabChatGPTDesc: Add as an app in ChatGPT · 3 steps · Plus, Pro, Team, Enterprise
quickstart.needAccount: You'll need a Telegram account on your phone with a recent Telegram client (so the QR-login option is available).
quickstart.claudeMetaDescription: Connect Telegram to Claude.ai in 5 steps via the Connectors menu. Read messages, search chats, get contacts.
quickstart.claudeIntro: Five steps. About thirty seconds. No API keys.
quickstart.claudeStep1Desc: Sign in to claude.ai and open Settings. Free, Pro, Max, and Team plans all support connectors.
quickstart.claudeStep2Desc: In Settings, find the Connectors section and click "Add custom connector".
quickstart.claudeStep3Desc: Enter the URL below in the connector dialog and click Connect.
quickstart.claudeStep4Desc: Claude.ai redirects to our OAuth consent screen. Click Approve, then a QR code appears. Open Telegram → Settings → Devices → Link Desktop Device → scan the QR.
quickstart.claudeStep5Desc: Claude.ai redirects back; you'll see a green "Connected" status. Ask it to read your chats: "Summarize my unread messages" works as a first prompt.
quickstart.claudeTroubleshootQRTitle: QR code expired or didn't scan
quickstart.claudeTroubleshootQRDesc: QR codes are valid for ~30 seconds. Refresh the connector dialog and try again. Make sure your phone has internet access while scanning.
quickstart.claudeTroubleshootDisconnectedDesc: Open the connector in Claude.ai and click Reconnect — you'll get a new QR. Sessions can also be revoked from Telegram → Settings → Devices.
quickstart.claudeTroubleshootChatsDesc: If Claude says you have no chats, your Telegram session likely needs reactivation. Disconnect and reconnect from claude.ai → Settings → Connectors.
quickstart.chatgptMetaDescription: Connect Telegram to ChatGPT in 3 steps via Apps Directory. Plus, Pro, Team, and Enterprise plans supported.
quickstart.chatgptIntro: Three steps. ChatGPT Plus, Pro, Team, or Enterprise required (Apps feature).
quickstart.chatgptStep1Desc: In ChatGPT Settings → Connectors → Advanced, toggle on Developer Mode. This lets you add custom MCP apps.
quickstart.chatgptStep2Desc: In Settings → Connectors → Create, choose I trust this application, paste the URL below, and click Create.
quickstart.chatgptStep3Desc: ChatGPT redirects to our OAuth screen. Approve, then scan the QR with Telegram → Settings → Devices → Link Desktop Device. ChatGPT redirects back and the app is ready.
quickstart.chatgptTroubleshootDoubleQRDesc: ChatGPT sometimes opens two parallel OAuth flows on first connect. Scan either QR — the second flow auto-redirects to the first session. Closing the duplicate tab is fine.
quickstart.chatgptTroubleshootLinkNotFoundDesc: ChatGPT doesn't auto-reconnect after server restarts. Disconnect and reconnect the app in ChatGPT Settings → Apps to re-establish the SSE stream.
quickstart.oauthDocsLink: See the OAuth reference for developers →

oauthDocs.metaDescription: Build a custom MCP client against mcp-telegram.com — RFC 6749/7591/7636/8252 OAuth with PKCE and loopback redirect support.
oauthDocs.heading: OAuth for custom MCP clients
oauthDocs.lead: If you're building your own MCP client (CLI, SDK, IDE plugin), this page describes our OAuth implementation: standards we support, endpoints, redirect_uri rules, and how to debug common errors. Claude.ai and ChatGPT users don't need this page — use the Quickstart instead.
oauthDocs.rfcLead: mcp-telegram.com is fully compliant with the OAuth specifications that the MCP ecosystem relies on — no proprietary extensions, no shared secrets baked into clients.
oauthDocs.rfc6749: OAuth 2.0 Authorization Framework — base authorization code grant with refresh tokens
oauthDocs.rfc7591: Dynamic Client Registration — any client can register itself at /oauth/register without prior coordination
oauthDocs.rfc7636: PKCE (Proof Key for Code Exchange) — S256 challenge required for public clients
oauthDocs.rfc8252: OAuth 2.0 for Native Apps — loopback IP redirect URIs with ephemeral port flexibility
oauthDocs.rfc8414: OAuth 2.0 Authorization Server Metadata — discovery document at /.well-known/oauth-authorization-server
oauthDocs.rfc9728: OAuth 2.0 Protected Resource Metadata — discovery of the MCP resource boundary
oauthDocs.flowLead: Standard RFC 6749 §4.1 + RFC 7636 flow. No surprises — if your OAuth library handles "authorization code + PKCE", it will work.
oauthDocs.flowStep1Desc: POST /oauth/register with { redirect_uris: ["http://127.0.0.1:<port>/callback"], client_name: "your-client-name" }. The server returns client_id + client_secret (the secret is optional for public PKCE clients but harmless to receive).
oauthDocs.flowStep2Desc: Generate a random 43-128 char code_verifier, then compute code_challenge = BASE64URL(SHA256(code_verifier)). Store the verifier locally for step 4.
oauthDocs.flowStep3Desc: Redirect the user to /oauth/authorize?response_type=code&client_id=...&redirect_uri=...&state=...&code_challenge=...&code_challenge_method=S256. The server displays a QR code; the user scans it in the Telegram app to authenticate.
oauthDocs.flowStep4Desc: After QR scan, the server redirects to your redirect_uri with ?code=...&state=.... Verify the state parameter matches what you sent.
oauthDocs.flowStep5Desc: POST /oauth/token with grant_type=authorization_code, code, redirect_uri, code_verifier, client_id. Receive an access_token (10-year TTL — see Token Lifetime below) and a refresh_token. Use the access_token as Authorization: Bearer ... on /mcp requests.
oauthDocs.redirectUriLead: We follow RFC 8252 §7.3 and §8.4 strictly. The matching algorithm depends on whether the registered URI is a loopback IP literal.
oauthDocs.redirectUriLoopbackDesc: If you registered a loopback URI, the authorize-time redirect_uri must match scheme, host, path, and query exactly — but the port may differ. This is required by RFC 8252 §7.3 because native clients bind an OS-assigned ephemeral port that may change between runs.
oauthDocs.redirectUriLoopbackRule2: Registered http://127.0.0.1:36201/callback does NOT match http://127.0.0.1:50000/different-path — path must be exact
oauthDocs.redirectUriLoopbackRule3: Registered http://[::1]:36201/cb does NOT match http://127.0.0.1:36201/cb — IPv4 and IPv6 loopback are separate identifiers
oauthDocs.redirectUriHttpsDesc: Exact byte-for-byte match required, including path, query, and port (RFC 6749 §3.1.2). No flexibility.
oauthDocs.redirectUriLocalhostDesc: We treat http://localhost as a regular hostname — exact match required, no port flexibility. RFC 8252 §8.3 recommends using IP literals (127.0.0.1 / [::1]) instead of localhost because DNS resolution is implementation-dependent.
oauthDocs.pkceDesc: code_challenge_method=S256 is required on every authorize request. Plain method is rejected. If you skip code_challenge entirely, the /token exchange will fail at code_verifier validation.
oauthDocs.tokenLifetimeDesc: access_token TTL is intentionally long (10 years) because some MCP clients do not persist refresh_token reliably. A refresh_token is still issued and rotates on every refresh (RFC 6819 §5.2.2.3). The user can revoke all tokens any time at /my/sessions or by logging out of Telegram. The user can also explicitly POST to /oauth/revoke (RFC 7009) to terminate a session.
oauthDocs.troubleshootInvalidRedirectDesc: The redirect_uri query parameter doesn't match any URI registered for this client_id. For loopback clients: check that scheme + host + path + query match exactly (only the port is flexible). For HTTPS clients: full byte-equality is required — watch for trailing slashes and URL-encoding differences.
oauthDocs.troubleshootUnknownClientDesc: The client_id doesn't exist in our database. Either you skipped the /oauth/register step, the registration response was lost before you saved the client_id, or the client was revoked by the user via /my/clients.
oauthDocs.troubleshootNeedsAuthDesc: If your client persists access_token but not refresh_token, you'll see this when the access_token expires. Our access tokens are 10-year TTL specifically to mitigate this, but if your client expires tokens client-side after some shorter window, you'll need to either persist refresh_token or call /oauth/revoke + re-auth on demand.
oauthDocs.testedClientsLead: Confirmed to interoperate with our server. If you build something new and it works, send us a PR to add it here.
oauthDocs.testedClientClaude: Claude.ai web — via built-in MCP connector
oauthDocs.testedClientChatGPT: ChatGPT Apps — via built-in MCP connector
oauthDocs.testedClientHermes: Hermes Agent — open-source CLI MCP client (RFC 8252 loopback flow)
oauthDocs.testedClientCursor: Cursor MCP — IDE plugin (RFC 8252 loopback flow)
oauthDocs.testedClientGeneric: Any RFC 6749 + RFC 7591 + RFC 7636 + RFC 8252 compliant client should work without code changes on our end.
oauthDocs.multiAccountHeading: Multiple Telegram accounts on one OAuth connection
oauthDocs.multiAccountLead: Since v2.32.0 a single OAuth connection can hold several Telegram identities and switch between them with one tool call — no Disconnect/Connect cycle, no new client registration.
oauthDocs.multiAccountStep1Desc: Call telegram-accounts-list. You will see your primary (OAuth-bound) account marked with ⭐ if it's active, plus any secondaries you've added.
oauthDocs.multiAccountStep2Desc: Call telegram-accounts-add with an optional label (e.g. "testing"). The tool returns a one-time URL (TTL 10 minutes) — open it on any device and scan the QR with the Telegram account you want to add.
oauthDocs.multiAccountStep3Desc: Call telegram-accounts-switch with identifier=label, @username, account_id, or 'primary'. The next telegram-* tool call uses that account immediately. No reconnect.
oauthDocs.multiAccountStep4Desc: Call telegram-accounts-remove identifier=… on a secondary. The Telegram account itself is NOT logged out — only the binding here. The primary cannot be removed this way; use your client's Disconnect flow to fully sign out.
oauthDocs.multiAccountSecurityNote: Each OAuth connection is isolated: accounts you attach via Hermes are invisible to Claude.ai or ChatGPT, even if it's the same Telegram identity. To connect different accounts to different MCP clients, register each client separately and use telegram-accounts-add inside its own session.

multiAccount.metaTitle: Connect multiple Telegram accounts to Claude AI & ChatGPT
multiAccount.metaDescription: Add several Telegram accounts to one AI connector and switch between them with one command — no disconnect/reconnect needed. Personal + work + testing in the same chat.
multiAccount.heading: Multiple Telegram accounts in one AI
multiAccount.intro: Connect once via the Quickstart, then attach additional Telegram accounts (personal, work, testing) to the same Claude AI or ChatGPT connector. Switch which account the next tool call uses with one command — no Disconnect/Connect cycle.
multiAccount.step1Desc: Finish the Quickstart for Claude AI or ChatGPT. The account you scan the QR with becomes your primary account — it's the one OAuth is bound to, marked ⭐ in the account list.
multiAccount.step2Title: Ask the AI to add another account
multiAccount.step2Desc: Say: "Add a second Telegram account, label it 'work'." The AI will call telegram-accounts-add and reply with a one-time URL. The URL is valid for 10 minutes and works on any device — open it in a browser to see a QR code.
multiAccount.step3Title: Scan the QR with the new account
multiAccount.step3Desc: Open Telegram on the phone with the account you want to add. Settings → Devices → Link Desktop Device → scan the QR. The account is linked, given the label you chose, and becomes active right away.
multiAccount.step4Desc: Say: "Switch to my primary account" or "Switch to the 'work' account." The AI calls telegram-accounts-switch and the next tool call uses that account. Use "list my Telegram accounts" to see what's attached.
multiAccount.step5Title: Detach an account when you're done
multiAccount.step5Desc: Say: "Remove the 'work' Telegram account." The AI calls telegram-accounts-remove. Only the binding here is removed — the Telegram account itself is NOT logged out. Your primary account cannot be removed this way; use the Disconnect flow in your AI client.
multiAccount.prompt1: List my Telegram accounts and tell me which one is active
multiAccount.prompt2: Add a new Telegram account, label it 'testing'
multiAccount.prompt3: Switch to @my_work_username and summarize unread messages
multiAccount.troubleshoot1Desc: Add-account URLs are single-use and expire after 10 minutes. Ask the AI to generate a new one with telegram-accounts-add.
multiAccount.troubleshoot2Title: Tried to add my primary account as a secondary
multiAccount.troubleshoot2Desc: The add-account flow refuses to bind the same Telegram identity as both primary and secondary — it would create a duplicate. Either scan with a different Telegram account, or use the existing primary directly (it's always available).
multiAccount.troubleshoot3Title: Switched but the next reply still uses the wrong account
multiAccount.troubleshoot3Desc: Confirm with "which Telegram account is active right now?" — the AI calls telegram-accounts-current and shows the live state. If a switch didn't stick, the identifier may have matched the wrong account; try the numeric account_id from the account list.

stories.metaTitle: Read and post Telegram Stories with Claude AI & ChatGPT
stories.metaDescription: Read stories from contacts and channels, see who viewed yours, post new ones, and pin highlights — all through Claude AI or ChatGPT.
stories.heading: Telegram Stories in your AI
stories.intro: Stories that contacts and channels you follow have posted, viewer lists for the stories you posted, and tools to post, pin, edit and delete your own — all available as AI tools.
stories.step1Desc: Say: "Show me active stories from people I follow." The AI calls telegram-get-all-stories and returns compact metadata (id, date, expire date, caption, media type, counters) for each story currently in your feed. Pagination is supported — ask for more to load older items.
stories.step2Desc: Say: "List viewers of my latest story." The AI calls telegram-get-story-views and returns viewers with their reaction emoji (if any) and view date, plus totals for views, forwards and reactions. Note: non-Premium accounts may not get a full viewer list, and very old stories may have lost their viewer data.
stories.step3Desc: Upload an image or short video first (open mcp-telegram.com/my/upload, drop the file, copy the uploadId) or pass an https:// URL the cloud can fetch. Then say: "Post a new story to my profile from this uploadId." The AI calls telegram-send-story. Privacy rules (everyone / contacts / close friends) are passed explicitly.
stories.step4Desc: Say: "Pin story 12345 to my profile." The AI calls telegram-toggle-story-pinned (up to 3 stories can be pinned). To edit a caption: "Change the caption of story 12345 to 'New caption'" — the AI calls telegram-edit-story. Replacing the media file is not supported in the cloud; post a fresh story instead.
stories.prompt1: Show me active stories from contacts, then read them aloud
stories.prompt2: Who viewed my last story? Group viewers by reaction emoji.
stories.prompt3: List my pinned stories and ask if I want to unpin any
stories.troubleshoot1Title: Empty viewer list on my story
stories.troubleshoot1Desc: Two common causes: (1) Telegram only retains the full viewer list for a limited time and very old stories may have lost it; (2) some accounts (non-Premium) do not get the full list at all. The totals (viewsCount, reactionsCount) are still returned.
stories.troubleshoot2Title: Can't change the media file in an existing story
stories.troubleshoot2Desc: telegram-edit-story can update caption and privacy rules, but the cloud explicitly refuses to replace the media file (it would require re-uploading bytes through filesystem). Delete the old story and post a fresh one instead.

uploads.metaTitle: Send files, voice notes and albums from Claude AI & ChatGPT to Telegram
uploads.metaDescription: Send documents, photos, voice notes and albums to any Telegram chat through Claude AI or ChatGPT — from your computer or directly from a URL.
uploads.heading: Send files & voice to Telegram
uploads.intro: Documents, photos, voice notes, video notes, albums, even stories and a new profile photo — anything that has bytes attached. The AI sends them on your behalf, either from a file you uploaded once, or directly from a public https:// URL.
uploads.step1Title: Pick how the bytes get in
uploads.step1Desc: Two paths: (1) upload a file once at mcp-telegram.com/my/upload, copy the returned uploadId, and reference it in your prompts; or (2) give the AI an https:// URL pointing to the file — the cloud will fetch it (with SSRF protection, so local/internal addresses are blocked). Max file size is around 50 MB.
uploads.step2Title: Send a single file or voice note
uploads.step2Desc: Say: "Send this PDF to @friend" with the uploadId or URL. The AI calls telegram-send-file. For voice messages (OGG/Opus preferred, M4A/MP3 also work) use telegram-send-voice. For round video messages use telegram-send-video-note.
uploads.step3Title: Send an album of 1-10 photos or videos
uploads.step3Desc: Say: "Send these 5 photos to my family chat as an album, with captions." The AI calls telegram-send-album. Each item gets its own uploadId-or-URL and optional caption. The first item's caption appears as the album caption in Telegram.
uploads.step4Desc: Say: "Set this as my Telegram profile photo" with an uploadId or URL. The AI calls telegram-set-profile-photo. Images and short MP4s both work. Use fallback:true if you want the photo shown when your account is private.
uploads.prompt1: Send the file at https://example.com/contract.pdf to @lawyer
uploads.prompt2: Make an album from the 4 photos I uploaded and post it to the family chat with the caption 'Weekend trip'
uploads.prompt3: Set my new profile photo from uploadId abc123
uploads.troubleshoot1Title: URL fetch failed with "address not allowed"
uploads.troubleshoot1Desc: The SSRF guard blocks URLs that resolve to private, link-local, loopback or metadata IP addresses. Use a public https:// URL, or upload the file first via /my/upload and reference the uploadId.
uploads.troubleshoot2Desc: Cloud uploads are capped around 50 MB. For larger files, host them on a public server and pass the https:// URL — Telegram itself supports up to 2 GB, the cloud limit is on the upload step only.
uploads.troubleshoot3Desc: Pending uploads are kept for a short window after /my/upload. If you took too long to use one, upload again and use the new uploadId.

privacyPage.title: Privacy Policy
privacyPage.metaDescription: Privacy policy for {brand} hosted Telegram MCP connector.

overview.heading: Overview
overview.body: {brand} (<host>{hostLabel}</host>) is a hosted connector that lets AI assistants (Claude, ChatGPT) access your Telegram account via the MCP protocol. Your privacy is important to us. This policy explains what data we collect, how we use it, and your rights.

0.desc: An encrypted session token is stored on our server so you stay connected between requests. It is deleted when you disconnect.

1.desc: We log which MCP tools are called (e.g. "list-chats", "read-messages"), the timestamp, and your Telegram user ID. We do not log message content, chat names, or any personal data from your chats.

2.desc: Temporary tokens for authenticating your AI client (Claude/ChatGPT) to our server. Stored in memory, not persisted.

analytics.heading: Website analytics
analytics.body: Our public website (not the MCP connector itself) uses Yandex.Metrika and Google Analytics to understand how visitors use the site. These tools set cookies and may record anonymized usage. They run only after you accept the consent banner — if you decline, no analytics scripts load and no cookies are set.

0.desc: Only the marketing/documentation website. Your Telegram data and MCP requests are never sent to any analytics service.

1.desc: Includes Webvisor (anonymized session replay of page interactions) and click maps. Form fields are masked by default; our pages contain no input forms with personal data.

2.desc: Decline the consent banner, clear the mcpt-consent cookie/localStorage to be asked again, or block analytics domains in your browser.

items.0: Message content, media files, or chat history
items.1: Phone numbers, contact lists, or profile data

dataFlow.heading: How your data flows
dataFlow.body: When you ask Claude or ChatGPT to read your Telegram messages, the AI client sends a request to our server. Our server fetches data from Telegram's API using your session, returns it to the AI client, and does not retain it. Message content passes through our server but is not stored or logged.

0.desc: Deleted when you disconnect or after inactivity.

1.desc: Retained for analytics and rate limiting. No personal content.

2.desc: In-memory only, cleared on server restart.

thirdParties.heading: Third parties
thirdParties.body: We do not sell, share, or transfer your Telegram data to third parties. Your Telegram data is only accessed via the official Telegram MTProto API on your behalf. The AI client (Anthropic/OpenAI) receives your Telegram data as part of the conversation — their privacy policies apply to that processing. Website analytics providers (Yandex, Google) receive only anonymized site-usage data, never your Telegram data.

security.heading: Security
security.body: All connections use TLS (HTTPS). Telegram sessions are encrypted. The server runs on dedicated infrastructure with access restricted to the operator. We follow security best practices for session management and credential storage.

0.desc: Remove the connector in Claude/ChatGPT settings. Your session is deleted immediately.

1.desc: Contact us to request full deletion of any stored data.

2.desc: Use the <repo>open-source version</repo> to run everything on your own machine with zero data leaving your device.

openSource.heading: Open source
openSource.body: The server is open source under the MIT license at <repo>{repoLabel}</repo>. You can inspect exactly what data is accessed and how.

contact.heading: Contact
contact.body: Questions about this policy? Reach out via <issues>{issuesLabel}</issues>
